title: Quantization harmonic noise probe and kernel interference notes
content:
Summary:

This working note captures an exploratory investigation into a subtle performance phenomenon we've observed in recent quantization experiments: low-amplitude, input-dependent latency/throughput oscillations that appear when certain quantization formats (INT8 / AWQ / GPTQ / FP8) are combined with specific kernel tiling and batching behaviors. I've been informally calling this effect 'harmonic noise' because it looks like a superimposed high-frequency ripple on throughput curves that correlates with activation distribution shifts during prefix-heavy workloads.

Why this matters:
- These micro-jitters inflate p95/p99 tails for some workloads without a commensurate drop in mean throughput, which makes SLO reasoning brittle.
- They can trigger autoscaler reactions or fallback logic unnecessarily, increasing cost and reducing stability.
- They appear to be kernel-sensitive — same quantization format with a different kernel selection shows materially different behavior.

Hypotheses (working):
1) Quantized activation dynamic range changes (per-layer or per-block) cause periodic cacheline/warp occupancy changes in some kernels leading to throughput ripples.
2) Mixed-precision paths (FP8 fallback in an INT8 pipeline) induce transient instruction mix shifts that align poorly with our CUDA kernel scheduler/SM utilization patterns.
3) Request prefix-length distribution interacts with KV-cache reuse patterns, exposing tiling micro-paths in certain matrix multiply kernels.

Experiment goals and success criteria:
- Reproduce the harmonic noise effect deterministically in a controlled microbench. Success = detectable periodic throughput oscillation in p50 vs p95 latency across runs on same machine image > 3x out of 5.
- Attribute to one of the hypotheses above via correlation to activation statistics, kernel occupancy, or instruction-level counters.
- Produce mitigations: kernel selection heuristic or small runtime shim to smooth out jitter (software warmup, minibatch smoothing, or quantization profile tweaks).

Setup (microbench harness):
- Models: rw-7b (base), rw-13b-inferred (bigger), small eval on rw-3b for faster iter.
- Quant formats: int8-gptq, int8-awq, fp8-e4m3, fp8-e5m2 (where available).
- Kernels: kernel-A (tiling 128x32, prefetch), kernel-B (128x64, vectorized lane-split), kernel-C (fallback generic matmul). These map to runtime kernel ids in the bench harness: K_A_128_32_v2, K_B_128_64_lane, K_C_generic_smcopy.
- Hardware: ampere-like GPU (m60 equivalently simulated), and heimdall cluster p3-class during booking windows. Machine: 8xA100-sim (dev box) + 1xA10 equivalent devnode for quick loops.
- Workloads: (a) short-prefix chat (prefix 10 tokens), (b) long-prefix retrieval (prefix 512 tokens), (c) bursty multi-turn trace extracted from prod-sample-2028-08 (sanitized).
- Batching regimes: single-request (no batching), dynamic batching (target batch 4, latency SLO 80ms), and continuous streaming (token-by-token).
- Metrics: p50/p75/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec throughput, GPU occupancy, L2 cache miss rates, warp efficiency, instruction mix (FP vs INT), perplexity change on held-out eval subset, log-prob delta (average).

Notes on harness changes made for this probe:
- Added per-token timestamping to isolate when jitter occurs within generation (prompt vs generation tokens).
- Hooked NVPROF-style counters (via CUPTI) for occupancy / L2 / global load/store counts at kernel granularity.
- Enabled fine-grained kernel pinning so we can force kernel-A/B/C for candidate conv blocks.

Initial observations (Sep 12-14 runs):
- Reproducible ripple seen on rw-7b quantized with AWQ (per-channel scales) when run with kernel-B under long-prefix workload. p95 latency oscillates between ~78ms and ~112ms in steady-state bursts (period ~18 requests), mean stays ~85ms.
- Same AWQ + kernel-A eliminates visible ripple; p95 ~88ms stable.
- FP8-e4m3 shows smaller amplitude oscillation under kernel-B but with less clear periodicity. GPTQ-int8 showed no ripple on kernel-C (generic), but degraded p50 slightly vs non-quant baseline.
- NV counters show correlated spikes in L2 miss rate and a drop in warp efficiency coincident with high-latency oscillation buckets.
- Activation histograms for affected layers show brief shifts in distribution mass crossing quantization bin boundaries at the same time windows where latency spikes occur (suggests scale/rescale boundary cases).

Quick numbers (example run rw-7b, long-prefix, dynamic batch target=4):
- Baseline fp32+kernel-A: p50=42ms p95=63ms tokens/s=4500
- AWQ+kernel-A: p50=40ms p95=70ms tokens/s=4700 (stable)
- AWQ+kernel-B: p50=39ms p95 median=95ms (oscillatory), tokens/s=4600 (but high p95 jitter)
- GPTQ+kernel-B: p50=41ms p95=74ms tokens/s=4550 (no oscillation)
- FP8+kernel-B: p50=38ms p95 ~85ms (mild oscillation)

Interpretation so far:
- Kernel-B's tiling/warp mapping seems sensitive to small shifts in activation sparsity / dynamic range. When activations cross a threshold (e.g., sign flip or scale boundary), memory access pattern changes and triggers a less efficient execution path or cacheline thrash.
- AWQ per-channel scales make those crossing points more frequent for certain prefix lengths because prefix tokens change token embedding context leading to activation variation.
- GPTQ's layout produces fewer boundary crossings (or quantizes in a way that is more stable under this distribution), hence fewer oscillations.

Open questions / things to test next:
- Is the effect device/architecture specific? (run same microbench on a different ISA/driver version).
- Are there thresholds in batch size that demarcate the onset of harmonics? (run batch sweep 1..16).
- Can small per-layer clip/fuzz during quantization reduce boundary crossings? (experiment: add +/-1% noise to scale factors at load time).
- Can kernel-B be patched to prefetch tile boundaries or to use a jitter-resistant lane assignment? (ask kernel owners Marco/Li).
- Does KV cache eviction timing align with the observed periods? (instrument cache lifecycle).

Proposed immediate mitigation (short-term):
1) Prefer kernel-A for AWQ on long-prefix routes in routing table as a conservative fallback (config flag).
2) Add a micro-warmup of 2 generation steps when switching quantized kernels for warm cache & stable activation history. This is cheap and may reduce transient states.
3) Add a lightweight monitoring probe that watches for periodic p95 spikes and flips the kernel steer to fallback after 3 occurrences in 30s.

Longer-term actions (R&D):
- Kernel-level: work with kernel owners to add metrics exposure and microarchitectural adjustments (tiling/prefetch heuristics) to reduce sensitivity to activation boundary changes.
- Quantization-level: sweep per-layer clip values and AWQ scale smoothing strategies to minimize crossing frequency. Consider hybrid per-block FP8 where AWQ unstable.
- Runtime-level: extend smart routing to route by workload prefix distribution and quantization profile (so long-prefix retrieval traffic prefers kernel/quant combos known to be stable).

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is an early working note. Numbers are from internal dev boxes, not final prod runs. The goal is to capture the reproducible pattern and a set of practical mitigations we can trial quickly.
- Please add experiments you think would isolate kernel internals (Marco may have lightweight kernel probes).

Relevant links and tickets (repeat here for convenience):
- PR: runtime#1345 (bench harness kernel pinning)
- Ticket: JIRA-ENG-5721 (quant-harmonics investigation)
- Confluence: Quant Harmonics Notes (internal)

Immediate next steps (owner assignments):
- Aisha: run batch-size sweep (1..16) on A100-dev by 2028-09-18, capture NV counters + activation hist profiles.
- Li Wei: add micro-prefetch toggle to kernel-B branch to test if it reduces L2 miss spikes (est 3d).
- Marco: expose per-kernel L1/L2 prefetch stats and lane assignment diagnostics (start PR 2d).
- Samira: prepare test routes that mirror long-prefix retrieval traffic for canary rollout (config + metrics).

Loose thoughts / TODOs (brainstorm style):
- Could we maintain two quantization scale versions (fast/robust) and switch based on observed activation variance?
- Explore small on-load jitter in scales to randomize boundary crossing and avoid lockstep periodicity (stochastic smoothing). Might hurt quality slightly; measure log-prob delta.
- Verify whether TPU-like matmul implementations show same harmonic noise (cross-vendor check).

End of note.
